elements.element: Restriction is mutual (binds both parties, not Customer alone)
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall directly solicit for employment any personnel of the other party"

elements.element: Scope limited to personnel directly involved in the services
elements.evidence: "personnel of the other party who are directly involved in the Services"

elements.element: Period runs from the end of that individual's involvement
elements.evidence: "after the end of that individual's involvement in the Services"

elements.element: Carve-out for general advertisements / general recruitment
elements.evidence: "hiring any person who responds to a general advertisement or other general recruitment activity not targeted at the other party's personnel"
"or who approaches that party on an unsolicited basis"
"neither party is subject to any no-hire obligation"; the original "solicit, hire, or employ" language is removed

elements.element: No non-solicit binding Customer at all (clause deleted or absent)
elements.evidence: § 12.4 as revised still binds Customer: "Neither party shall directly solicit for employment any personnel of the other party"

reasons: The revised § 12.4 satisfies every atomic element of the fallback: mutuality, limitation to personnel directly involved in the Services, a twelve-month period measured from the end of that individual's involvement, general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and express negation of any no-hire obligation.

The preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer) is not achieved because a mutual restriction still binds Customer, but the drafter's locked target level is fallback, so this is acceptable and the clause sits at the fallback.

The official duration and unsolicited-approach checks appear to be literal-pattern artefacts ("twelve" spelled out rather than "12"); the operative words "for twelve months after the end of that individual's involvement in the Services" and "who approaches that party on an unsolicited basis" expressly supply both requirements.

Although the operation is a full sentence replacement flagged by the size gate, the original sentence was a one-directional 24-month no-hire; mutuality, scope narrowing, the measurement trigger, two carve-outs and the no-hire negation cannot be achieved by changing a number or operator, so the rewrite is no broader than needed.

No unrelated term is disturbed: § 12.3 is untouched and the revision removes the prior contradiction with Vendor's acknowledgement that Customer gave no no-hire commitment; no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
